source.title: Surgical Refusal Ablation: Disentangling Safety from Intelligence via Concept-Guided Spectral Cleaning

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares raw contrastive refusal-vector ablation with a cleaned, concept-residualized intervention and argues that the raw vector is polysemantic and can cause collateral drift. Its results refine the single-direction account.
record.gate_note: The paper reports refusal rates, distribution-drift metrics, capability perplexity, and measurements of refusal-vector overlap/components. The concept-atom and layer choices are not recorded as outcome rows when used only to construct the intervention.
record.test_reason: The study ablates the raw harmful-minus-harmless direction in five instruct models and reports refusal rates and WT2 drift. It compares this with a residualized, iterative rank-one weight edit (SRA). The results bear on V1's removal and ability-preservation parts, on V2, and weakly on V4 through the multi-pass refusal components.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also stress that standard ablation fails to fully remove refusal in the larger models (Qwen3-VL-8B, Ministral-14B). They attribute standard-ablation damage to 'Ghost Noise' from a polysemantic vector, not to an inherent safety–capability trade-off.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation contrast to form a raw direction, but residualizes it against curated Shield and Confound atoms and applies rank-one weight updates to selected projection matrices/layers. The study also compares a Standard ablation. It does not test adding the direction or the original all-layer/all-position activation projection recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome differs by model and intervention: Standard ablation leaves substantial refusal on Qwen3-VL-8B and Ministral-14B and causes larger WT2 KL drift than SRA. The paper also reports changing semantic components over iterative passes on Qwen3-VL-2B at Layer 25.

fits_no_version.finding: In Qwen3-VL-2B, the raw difference-in-means refusal vector has cosine about −0.22 with a Logic atom and +0.18 with a Coding atom. Section 4.2 says it suppresses Shields nearly as strongly as Targets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The difference-in-means refusal direction is contaminated with capability/style directions, and removing them reduces ablation side-effects.

record.problems: The paper itself notes that refusal detection is definition-dependent, harmful prompt suites are finite, the curated atom registry may miss confounds, and WT2 perplexity/first-token KL and GSM8K/MBPP perplexity are proxies rather than comprehensive behavioral capability evaluations. No uncertainty estimates are reported in the presented results.
record.rows_left_out: None of the separately reported numeric results relevant to the tested versions were left out.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal. The exact all-layer, all-position projection recipe. Downstream task accuracy.
Whether the Standard baseline is itself a weight edit; public abliterated checkpoints.
Formal comparison of affine, cone, and multi-direction models of refusal.

missing.what: Projection magnitudes of Standard vs SRA vectors on Target, Shield and Style atoms; per-layer heatmap values.
Number of SRA passes and layers used per model, and the Standard ablation's layers and implementation.

record.verdict_notes: Single-author preprint with no uncertainty estimates, an automated refusal rubric, and a finite suite (about 112 prompts). SRA also uses iterative hard-negative re-mining, so its gains over Standard confound cleaning with iteration. Capability is measured only by perplexity and first-token KL proxies.

versions.untested_parts: Tests removal interventions and reports refusal and proxy capability outcomes; does not test adding the direction to induce harmless-request refusals, ablation at every layer and position, or comprehensive general capability.
Tests weight-edit ablations on the named instruct models; does not establish that the edits are a released or generally deployed abliteration procedure.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Reports entanglement and changing semantic components in the raw direction; does not compare affine, cone, and dominant-direction models as formal alternatives.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
Does not test cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer.
Does not vary refusal-training method or timing.
Does not test reasoning models as a category or compare reasoning and non-reasoning models.

relation.reason: Ablates the harmful-minus-harmless direction on five instruct models and reports refusal and drift results that bear on V1/V2.

tranche.reason: The study's own Table 1 shows raw-direction ablation leaving 42%/12% refusal in the larger models and causing WT2 drift (KL up to 2.088). It argues the raw vector is polysemantic and V1's 'abilities kept' needs restating (Sec 1, 6.1, 6.2).

source_check.notes: Single-author preprint with no code, seeds or uncertainty. The refusal judge is an unspecified 'automated rubric' on a harmful suite of 'e.g., 112' prompts. The layers, positions and implementation of 'Standard' ablation are never described. Table 2 (GSM8K/MBPP) compares only Base and SRA, with no Standard arm. On Ministral-3B, Standard beats SRA on refusal (0.0 vs 2.0%) and dPPL (+0.050 vs +0.060). Rows r01/r03/r07 are linked to V2, but no V2 verdict uses them.

statements.correction: Add size steps for 2601.08489: Qwen3-VL 2B/4B->8B and Ministral 3B->14B. The study gives one run per model with no uncertainty, and 'Standard' ablation layers and implementation are not described.
statements.problem: None for this study. 93.8->42.0 (Qwen3-VL-8B), 91.9->12.0 (Ministral-14B) and 0.0% for Qwen3-VL-2B/4B and Ministral-3B are all in Table 1. The scaling explanation is the authors' hypothesis in Sec 6.2. The conditions field does not list this study's size steps (2B/4B->8B, 3B->14B).

statements.correction: SRA = ridge-residualized DIM direction plus iterative hard-negative re-mining over several passes (about 4 on Qwen3-VL-2B L25), with rank-one updates to selected MLP/attention matrices. Five models: 0.0/0.0/2.0/2.0/0.0%.
statements.problem: Numbers are correct (83.3->0.0, 93.8->2.0, 91.9->0.0; range 83-96% -> 0-2%). 'Rank-one SRA' leaves out that SRA is iterative: rank-one updates on selected matrices in several layers (e.g. 15-25), with the direction re-mined from still-refused prompts on each pass.

statements.correction: 2601.08489 Standard vs SRA refusal: Qwen3-VL-2B 0.0 vs 0.0; 4B 0.0 vs 0.0; 8B 42.0 vs 2.0; Ministral-3B 0.0 vs 2.0; Ministral-14B 12.0 vs 0.0. Standard's residual refusal appears only in the two largest models.
statements.problem: The 42.0% vs 2.0% on Qwen3-VL-8B is correct. But in this study the plain form does not generally remove less: Standard equals SRA on Qwen3-VL-2B/4B (0.0% each) and beats it on Ministral-3B (0.0% vs 2.0%). The paper also calls SRA 'Surgical Refusal Ablation', not abliteration, and never specifies how 'Standard' is implemented.

statements.correction: Gap only in Qwen3-VL-8B (42.0 vs 2.0) and Ministral-14B (12.0 vs 0.0). Equal or reversed on the 2-4B models (Ministral-3B 0.0 vs 2.0).
statements.problem: Numbers are correct. The gap appears only in the 8B and 14B models. Standard and SRA also differ in more than direction extraction: SRA adds iterative hard-negative re-mining and gamma-scaled edits on selected matrices, while Standard's implementation is not described.
